_comment: C6-8 正文英译 · intercom-mcp（2026-10-31）。八维+mcp 三维+runs/unknowns/related/sources 全键非空。

axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an official hosted remote server called by MCP clients. One exception wording: the **Fin Operator tool family**
drives Intercom's own AI (Operator) to work — send_operator_message consumes Operator credits
(billed the same way as starting a turn inside Intercom), while the other four Operator tools are free.
axes.local_files: Reads and writes no local files — the read/write objects all live on the Intercom workspace side (conversations/contacts/companies/Help Center articles).
axes.background: No persistent local background; the connection lives between the client and Intercom's hosted endpoint (official wording: the connection stays live to receive updates).
axes.context:
No server-side cross-session memory; the context is your Intercom workspace data itself (official narrative: AI assistants keep awareness of your workspace).
Operator chats have server-side session state (get_operator_response collects the answer later).
axes.permissions:
**Two authentication modes**: OAuth (recommended; Dynamic Client Registration, but every registered redirect URI passes an allowlist —
localhost/127.0.0.1 on any port is already allowed, other callbacks must be requested first) or Bearer token (an Intercom API token,
with scopes: read users/companies, read conversations, read+write articles).
**Bearer connections do not get the Fin Operator tools** (stated plainly by the official docs); connections made before the Operator permission existed must reconnect.
Tools are authorized as you — mirroring your own workspace permissions, MCP grants no extra rights.
axes.fit:
Fits: support teams plugging Intercom data into AI tools (Claude/Cursor/VS Code and other officially listed clients) —
querying conversations and contacts, reading and writing Help Center docs, driving Operator; EU workspaces get a data-residency line.
Not a fit: AU-hosted workspaces (unsupported); wanting a self-hosted/open-source implementation (none); wanting Bearer simplicity while also using Operator (you won't get it).

mcp.transport:
**streamable-http** (recommended: US https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp, EU https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp)
+ **legacy SSE** (/sse, marked deprecated by the official docs, kept only for backwards compatibility).
Verified: the mcp.intercom.com landing page and developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/mcp (200 direct on 2026-10-31; endpoints 401 direct = exist, auth required).
mcp.auth:
OAuth (recommended; DCR + redirect-URI allowlist) or Bearer token (API token + scopes: read users/companies, read conversations, read+write articles).
Tool authorization mirrors your own workspace permissions — MCP grants no extra rights.
mcp.scope:
Read surface (conversations/contacts/companies/articles) + **write surface** (Help Center article create/update,
Operator apply_proposals changing live workspace configuration); no local surface. The write surface is gated by workspace permissions and proposal approval.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The full parameter surface of the 14 tools and the pagination-cursor semantics in detail (the docs are thorough; not enumerated item by item)
- Operator credit pricing and quota numbers (per D9 and snapshot discipline no numbers are recorded)
- The support timeline for AU-hosted workspaces (the official docs only say not yet supported)
related: A customer-support vertical vs a thousand-app hub: Intercom is an official single-product deep integration, Zapier is a cross-application entry point.
Both are official SaaS remote servers: Atlassian covers tickets/knowledge, Intercom covers customer conversations plus Help Center read-and-write.
